source.author: Ptolemy
source.edition: F. E. Robbins (1940), Tetrabiblos III.13, Loeb pp 333–363, editor note 151
source.read_scope: Complete III.13 paragraphs 23–64; five planetary solitary rulers and ten alliances; Sun and Moon are modifiers rather than additional solitary character lists.

rational.inquiry: Regularly seeks explanations or investigates unfamiliar questions beyond immediate necessity
rational.invention: Regularly devises new methods, mechanisms or solutions rather than only following instructions
rational.learning: Regularly pursues acquisition of knowledge or sustained study
rational.detail: Regularly checks precise details or works painstakingly when undertaking an important task
rational.practical: Regularly organizes practical affairs and translates plans into implemented actions
rational.work: Regularly sustains effort on meaningful tasks rather than avoiding labor
rational.firmness: Typically maintains a settled purpose or position despite ordinary opposition
rational.change_mind: Frequently changes a settled view or purpose over time; distinct from revising a method
rational.deliberation: Typically considers consequences before consequential decisions rather than acting precipitately
rational.discussion: Regularly engages in reasoned intellectual discussion
rational.eloquence: Can communicate ideas in a fluent, effective manner; not a claim about sales or lying
rational.talk: Typically speaks at length in ordinary interactions
rational.aspiration: Regularly pursues far-reaching achievements or recognition; do not infer desire for formal office
rational.faith_practice: Regularly engages in religious or contemplative practices; no supernatural accuracy claim
rational.reflection: Regularly engages in sustained reflection on important or abstract questions rather than accepting an immediate answer

sensory_affective.leadership: Typically takes command or directing authority when a group needs direction
sensory_affective.confrontation: Regularly initiates or sustains confrontations and quarrels in disagreements
sensory_affective.anger: Frequently becomes overtly angry quickly in ordinary provocation
sensory_affective.harshness: Typically treats others sternly or harshly in ordinary conflict
sensory_affective.compassion: Regularly responds to the distress of others with concrete help or consideration
sensory_affective.generosity: Regularly gives resources, money or time to others beyond an immediate obligation
sensory_affective.sociability: Regularly seeks or readily engages in friendly company
sensory_affective.solitude: Regularly prefers time alone over company
sensory_affective.trust_caution: Typically suspects possible misconduct or deception before clear proof in ordinary relationships
sensory_affective.frankness: Typically communicates intentions or opinions openly and directly
sensory_affective.self_restraint: Typically restrains strong immediate desires or impulses when they conflict with commitments
sensory_affective.pleasure: Regularly prioritizes enjoyable or sensory experiences
sensory_affective.aesthetic: Regularly pursues art, beauty or aesthetic appreciation
sensory_affective.lavish_spending: Regularly spends resources lavishly or beyond planned practical limits
sensory_affective.boasting: Regularly boasts about own achievements or status
sensory_affective.faultfinding: Regularly criticizes faults in others or their conduct
sensory_affective.deception: Repeatedly knowingly misrepresents facts to others in pursuit of advantage
sensory_affective.reliability: Typically keeps agreements and promises even when inconvenient
sensory_affective.modesty: Typically avoids elevating own status or displaying superiority
sensory_affective.risk: Regularly chooses ventures with meaningful uncertainty or potential loss
sensory_affective.cheerfulness: Typically behaves cheerfully or playfully during ordinary interactions
sensory_affective.timidity: Frequently hesitates to act in ordinary situations primarily because of fear or lack of confidence

limitations: The assigned directions are narrow modern hypotheses, not an exhaustive lexical transcription. Omitted descriptors contribute no score. Position conditions are not moral valence; both clauses may contain undesirable behavior.

No original exact numerical qualification or alliance criterion is supplied. Separate-place use of single-planet profiles and joint use of pair profiles are competing conditional experimental models; neither is represented as the complete historical rule.
Sun and Moon possible top candidates are preserved as abstentions in the character mapping rather than replaced by another body.

No trait is assumed absent merely because a chart lacks the carrier. Explicit negative behavior must be supported by the respondent. No disease, identity, criminality or supernatural skill is inferred.
condition_policy: Both source position clauses retained. No proxy asserts dignity or adverse status. Separate and assumed-alliance models use identical, predeclared observation denominators.
